O Allah, protect me from before me, from behind me, from my right, from my left, and from above me. And I seek refuge in Your Magnificence lest I be destroyed suddenly from beneath me."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1206; Arabic Hadith: 1206

Sayyiduna Anas ibn Mālik (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever says in the morning: 'O Allāh, we have reached the morning, and we call You as witness, and we call the bearers of Your Throne, Your other angels, and all of Your creation as witnesses that You are Allāh, there is no deity worthy of worship except You, You alone, without any partner, and indeed Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) is Your servant and Your Messenger' — Allāh, the Most High, shall free one-fourth of him from the Hellfire on that day. And if he says it twice, Allāh shall free half of him from the Hellfire. And if he says it four times, Allāh shall free him entirely from the Hellfire on that day."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1207; Arabic Hadith: 1207*

Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that Sayyiduna Abū Bakr (may Allāh be pleased with him) submitted: "O Messenger of Allāh! Teach me a supplication that I may recite in the morning and evening." He (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Recite: 'O Allāh, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Lord and Sovereign of all things. I bear witness that there is no deity worthy of worship except You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own self, from the evil of Shayṭān, and from his shirk (associating partners with You).' Recite this in the morning, in the evening, and when you go to sleep."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1208; Arabic Hadith: 1208*

Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates in a similar manner to the first hadith. The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Lord and Sovereign of all things." And he also said: "From the evil of Shayṭān and from his shirk."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1209; Arabic Hadith: 1209*

Abū Rāshid Ḥibrānī (may Allāh have mercy on him) narrates: "I came into the presence of Sayyiduna ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr (may Allāh be pleased with them both) and requested: 'Narrate to me a hadith that you heard from the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him).' He handed me a scroll and said: 'This is the scroll that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) wrote for me.' I looked at it and found therein: 'Indeed, Sayyiduna Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq (may Allāh be pleased with him) asked the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him): "O Messenger of Allāh! Teach me a supplication that I may recite in the morning and evening." The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "O Abū Bakr, recite: 'O Allāh, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Sovereign of all things. I seek refuge in You from the evil of my own self, from the evil of Shayṭān and his shirk, and from committing any wrong against my own soul or causing harm to any Muslim.'"

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1210; Arabic Hadith: 1210*

Sayyiduna Ḥudhayfah (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) intended to sleep, he would say: "In Your name, O Allāh, I die and I live." And when he awoke from sleep, he would say: "All praise is due to Allāh, Who gave us life after causing us to die, and unto Him is the resurrection."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1211; Arabic Hadith: 1211*

Sayyiduna Anas (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that when the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) came to his bed, he would recite this supplication: "All praise is due to Allāh, Who fed us, gave us drink, sufficed us, and provided us with shelter — and how many are those who have none to suffice them or provide them shelter."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1212; Arabic Hadith: 1212*

Sayyiduna Jābir (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) would never sleep without first reciting Sūrah al-Sajdah and Sūrah al-Mulk. Abū Zubayr says: "These two sūrahs possess a merit exceeding that of every other sūrah of the Noble Qur'ān by seventy virtues. Whoever recites both of them shall have seventy good deeds recorded for him, seventy ranks elevated for him, and seventy sins erased through them."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1213; Arabic Hadith: 1213*

Sayyiduna ʿAbdullāh (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates, saying: "Sleep at the time of dhikr (remembrance) comes from Shayṭān. If you wish, you may test this. When any one of you goes to his bed and intends to sleep, let him remember Allāh, the Mighty and Majestic."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1214; Arabic Hadith: 1214*

Sayyiduna Jābir (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) would not sleep until he had completed the recitation of Sūrah al-Mulk and Alīm Sajdah (Sūrah al-Sajdah).

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1215; Arabic Hadith: 1215*

Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When any one of you lies down on his bed, let him shake out the inner garment of his lower garment and dust off his bed with it, for he does not know what may have settled on it after he left it. And it is fitting that he lie on his right side and recite this supplication: 'In Your name, O Allāh, I have placed my side (on this bed). So if You take my soul, have mercy upon it, and if You release it, then protect it in the manner in which You protect the righteous among Your servants.'" Or he said: "…in the manner in which You protect Your righteous servants."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1216; Arabic Hadith: 1216*

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Barā' ibn 'Āzib (may Allāh be pleased with them both) that when the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) would go to his bed, he would lie on his right side and then recite this supplication: "O Allāh, I have directed my face toward You, and I have entrusted my soul to You, and I have placed my reliance upon You, out of hope for Your bounty and fear of Your punishment. There is no place of refuge and no sanctuary besides You. I have believed in the Book which You have revealed and in the Prophet whom You have sent." Then he (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "Whoever recites these words (with faith and conviction) during the night and then passes away that same night, his death shall be upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) that when the Messenger of Allāh (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) would lie down on his bed, he would recite: "O Allāh, Lord of the heavens and the earth, Sovereign of all things, Splitter of the grain and the seed, Revealer of the Tawrāh, the Injīl, and the Qur'ān. I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil thing whose forelock is in Your Hand. You are the First—nothing is before You. You are the Last—nothing is after You. You are the Manifest—nothing is above You. You are the Hidden—nothing is beyond You. Settle my debt and enrich me, so that I may be free from want."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Barā' ibn 'Āzib (may Allāh be pleased with them both) that when the Messenger of Allāh (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) would come to his bed, he would lie on his right side and then recite: "O Allāh, I have entrusted my soul to You, I have directed my face toward You, I have consigned my affair to You, and I have placed my reliance upon You in all my matters, out of hope in You and fear of You. There is no place of refuge and no sanctuary for me besides You. I have believed in the Book which You have revealed and in the Messenger whom You have sent." The Messenger of Allāh (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "Whoever recites these words and then passes away that same night, his death shall have come upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah)."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Jābir (may Allāh be pleased with him), who said: When a person enters his house or goes to his bed, an angel and a devil hasten toward him. The angel says: "End your affair with goodness," and the devil says: "End your affair with evil." If he then praises and remembers Allāh, the angel repels the devil and guards him throughout the night. When he awakens, the angel and the devil again hasten toward him, and the same exchange takes place. If he remembers Allāh and says: "All praise belongs to the One who returned my soul to me after death and did not cause it to die in its sleep. All praise belongs to the One who keeps the heavens and the earth from moving out of their places—if they were to move, who could hold them after Him? Indeed, He is the Most Forgiving, the Most Pardoning. All praise belongs to the One who keeps the heavens from falling upon the earth except by His permission—indeed, He is the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful." If he passes away (in that state), he dies upon martyrdom, and if he rises and performs ṣalāh, it is a prayer of great virtue.

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Barā' (may Allāh be pleased with him) that when the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) intended to sleep, he would place his hand beneath his right cheek and recite: "O Allāh, protect me from the punishment of the Day on which You will raise Your servants." It is also narrated from Sayyiduna Barā' through another chain in a similar manner.

It is narrated by Sayyiduna 'Abdullāh ibn 'Amr (may Allāh be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "Whoever adheres to two practices shall certainly enter Paradise. They are both easy, and those who act upon them are few." It was asked: "O Messenger of Allāh, what are they?" He (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "After every ṣalāh, one should recite 'Allāhu Akbar' ten times, 'Alḥamdulillāh' ten times, and 'Subḥānallāh' ten times. That totals one hundred and fifty upon the tongue and one thousand five hundred on the Scale." I (the narrator) saw the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) counting them on his hand. And when he went to his bed, he would recite 'Subḥānallāh' thirty-three times, 'Alḥamdulillāh' thirty-three times, and 'Allāhu Akbar' thirty-four times—that is one hundred upon the tongue and one thousand on the Scale. "Which of you commits two hundred and fifty sins in a day and night?" It was asked: "O Messenger of Allāh, how can a person not act upon this?" He said: "The devil comes to one of you during his ṣalāh and reminds him of various worldly matters, so that he does not remember these glorifications."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "When any of you goes to his bed, let him take the inner part of his lower garment and dust the bed with it, and recite 'Bismillāh,' for he does not know what has come upon the bed after he left it. Then, when he intends to lie down, let him lie on his right side and recite: 'O my Lord, pure is Your name. By Your name I lay myself down, and by Your grace I shall rise. If You take my soul, then forgive it; and if You release it, then guard it as You guard Your righteous servants.'"

It is narrated by Rabi'ah ibn Ka'b (may Allāh be pleased with him) that I used to spend the night at the door of the Prophet's (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) house so that I could provide him with water for wuḍū' and other needs. I would hear him at length during the night reciting "Sami' Allāhu li-man ḥamidah" and at length reciting "Alḥamdulillāhi Rabbil-'Ālamīn."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Ibn 'Abbās (may Allāh be pleased with them both) that the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "Whoever falls asleep while his hands are greasy (with food) and does not wash them, and then something (harmful) bites him, let him blame none but himself."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abū Hurayrah (may Allāh be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ṣallallāhu 'alayhi wa sallam) said: "Whoever sleeps with greasy hands and then something (harmful) bites him, let him blame none but himself."

Sayyidunā Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "At night, close the doors, tie the mouths of the water-skins, overturn the vessels or cover them, and extinguish the lamps. For indeed, Shayṭān does not open a closed door, nor does he untie a water-skin, nor does he uncover a covered vessel. And verily, the mouse is a wicked creature that sets people's houses on fire."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1227 | Arabic Hadith: 1227

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them both) narrates. He said: A mouse came and began pulling the wick of the lamp. A girl went to stop it, but the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Leave it." So the mouse brought the wick and placed it upon the mat on which he was reclining. An area of the mat the size of a dirham was burned. The Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) then said: "When you go to sleep, extinguish your lamps, for indeed, Shayṭān instructs such creatures in such matters, and they set you on fire."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1228 | Arabic Hadith: 1228

Abū Saʿīd (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates. He said: One night the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) was awake. He suddenly saw a mouse climbing onto the roof carrying a wick so as to set the house on fire. Thereupon, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) cursed it and declared its killing permissible even within the sacred precinct (Ḥaram).
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1229 | Arabic Hadith: 1229

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with them both) narrates that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Do not leave fire burning in your houses when you go to sleep."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1230 | Arabic Hadith: 1230

Sayyidunā ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with him) said: "Indeed, fire is an enemy, so beware of it." Consequently, Sayyidunā Ibn ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with them both) was especially vigilant regarding fire in his house and would extinguish it before going to sleep.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1231 | Arabic Hadith: 1231

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿUmar (may Allāh be pleased with them both) narrates that he heard the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) saying: "Do not leave fire burning in your houses (at night), for it is an enemy."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1232 | Arabic Hadith: 1232

Sayyidunā Abū Mūsā (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates. He said: One night, a house in Madīnah al-Ṭayyibah was set ablaze along with its inhabitants. When this was mentioned to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), he said: "This fire is your enemy. Therefore, when you go to sleep, extinguish it."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1233 | Arabic Hadith: 1233

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that when rain would descend, he would say: "O girl! Take out my saddle and my clothes." And he would recite: "And We sent down from the sky blessed water." (Qāf, 50:9)
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1234 | Arabic Hadith: 1234

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿAbbās (may Allāh be pleased with them both) narrates that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) commanded that refuse be hung inside the house.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1235 | Arabic Hadith: 1235

Sayyidunā Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh (may Allāh be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When night falls and stillness prevails, reduce your movement, for none among you knows which of Allāh's creatures the Almighty spreads abroad. Close the doors, tie the mouths of the water-skins, cover the vessels, and extinguish the lamps."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1236 | Arabic Hadith: 1236

Sayyiduna Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Keep your children close to you until the early part of the evening passes. That is the time when the devils spread out."

narrator: 'Umar said, "Sometimes some of the men of Quraysh sat at the door of Ibn Mas'ud. When the shadows shifted from west to east, he said, 'Get up, Any time spent here after this is for Shaytan.' He made everyone he passed by get up. While we were getting up, someone said to him, 'This is the mawla of the Banu'l-Hashas who composes poetry.' 'Umar called and said, 'What have you got to say?' The man said:
in_book_reference: Book 52, Hadith 1 English translation : Book 52, Hadith 1238
text:
'Say farewell to Salma if you prepare to go in the morning,
       White hair and Islam is enough prohibition for a man'

'Umar said, 'Enough! You have spoken the truth. You have spoken the truth.'"

As-Sa'ib ibn Yazid said, "'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him,
used to pass by us in the middle of the day - or near to it - and
say, 'Get up and take a midday nap. Any time spent here after this is for
shaytan.'"

Anas said, "At the time that wine was made unlawful, there was
no drink that the people of Madina liked better than that made from dried
dates and unripe dates. I used to give the drink to the Companions of the
Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They were
in the home of Abu Talha when a man passed by and announced, 'Wine has
been forbidden.' They did not say, 'When?' or 'Wait until we see.' They
said, 'Anas, break them!' Then they said in the presence of Umm Sulaym,
'Wait until it becomes cool and we have washed ourselves.' Then Umm Sulaym
put perfume on them. Then they went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him
and grant him peace, and the news was as the man had said."

Anas said, "At the time that wine was made unlawful, there was
no drink that the people of Madina liked better than that made from dried
dates and unripe dates. I used to give the drink to the Companions of the
Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. They were
in the home of Abu Talha when a man passed by and announced, 'Wine has
been forbidden.' They did not say, 'When?' or 'Wait until we see.' They
said, 'Anas, break them!' Then they said in the presence of Umm Sulaym,
'Wait until it becomes cool and we have washed ourselves.' Then Umm Sulaym
put perfume on them. Then they went to the Prophet, may Allah bless him
and grant him peace, and the news was as the man had said."

حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ ثَابِتٍ، قَالَ أَنَسٌ‏:‏ مَا كَانَ لأَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ شَرَابٌ، حَيْثُ حُرِّمَتِ الْخَمْرُ، أَعْجَبَ إِلَيْهِمْ مِنَ التَّمْرِ وَالْبُسْرِ، فَإِنِّي لَأَسْقِي أَصْحَابَ رَسُولِ اللهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم، وَهُمْ عِنْدَ أَبِي طَلْحَةَ، مَرَّ رَجُلٌ فَقَالَ‏:‏ إِنَّ الْخَمْرَ قَدْ حُرِّمَتْ، فَمَا قَالُوا‏:‏ مَتَى‏؟‏ أَوْ حَتَّى نَنْظُرَ، قَالُوا‏:‏ يَا أَنَسُ، أَهْرِقْهَا، ثُمَّ قَالُوا عِنْدَ أُمِّ سُلَيْمٍ حَتَّى أَبْرَدُوا وَاغْتَسَلُوا، ثُمَّ طَيَّبَتْهُمْ أُمُّ سُلَيْمٍ، ثُمَّ رَاحُوا إِلَى النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم، فَإِذَا الْخَبَرُ كَمَا قَالَ الرَّجُلُ‏.‏
قَالَ أَنَسٌ‏:‏ فَمَا طَعِمُوهَا بَعْدُ‏.‏

in_book_reference: Book 52, Hadith 5 English translation : Book 52, Hadith 1242
text: Khawwat ibn Jubayr said, "Sleep at the beginning of the day is stupidity, in the middle of it is (an act of) character,and at the end of it is imbecility."

Maymun (ibn Mahran) said, "I asked Nafi', 'Did Ibn 'Umar ever
invite people to a banquet?' He said, 'A camel of his once broke something
and so we sacrificed it. Then Ibn 'Umar said, "Gather the people of Madina
for me." I said, "Abu 'Abdu'r-Rahman, for what? We do not have any bread."
He said, "O Allah, praise belongs to You. These are bits of meat and this
is broth," or he said, "Broth and meat chunks. Whoever wishes can eat and
whoever wishes can leave it."'"

Sa'ib ibn Yazid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates that Sayyiduna Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Some people from Quraysh would stand at the door of Sayyiduna Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) — so that they might learn something — when the shadow began to decline, he would say: 'Rise now, for the time that remains is for the Shaytan.' Then he would pass by them and forcefully make them get up. While they were thus engaged, it was said to them: 'This is a slave of Banu Hushaysh who recites poetry.' They called him and asked: 'What poetry did you recite?' He said: 'If you have resolved upon a morning journey, then leave Salim, for old age and the religion of Islam are sufficient to keep a person from evil.' He (Ibn Mas'ud) said: 'Enough, you have spoken the truth, you have spoken the truth.'"

Sa'ib ibn Yazid (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates, he said: "Sayyiduna Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) would pass by us around midday and say: 'Rise and take a siqaylah (afternoon nap), for the time that remains is for the Shaytan.'"
Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that he would perform the Friday prayer and then take a siqaylah (afternoon nap).

Sayyiduna Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates: "When the prohibition of wine was revealed, the preferred wine of the people of Madinah was made from dried dates and fresh dates. One day, I was serving wine to the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) at the house of Abu Talhah (may Allah be pleased with him), when a man passed by and said: 'Wine has been made unlawful.' He (Abu Talhah) did not ask when it had become unlawful or investigate the matter; rather he said: 'O Anas, pour this wine away.' Then he took a siqaylah (afternoon nap) at the house of Umm Sulaym until the intensity of the sun diminished, and he performed ghusl (ritual bath). Then Umm Sulaym (may Allah be pleased with her) applied perfume to him. Then he came into the presence of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him), and the situation was just as the man had described. Sayyiduna Anas (may Allah be pleased with him) says: 'After that, he never again put wine to his lips.'"

Khawwat ibn Jubayr (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates, he said: "Sleep during the first part of the day is ignorance, sleeping during the middle part is a good habit, and sleeping during the latter part is foolishness."

Maymun ibn Mahran (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates: "I asked Nafi' (may Allah have mercy on him) whether Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) would invite people to feasts. He said: 'It was not the general practice, but once his camel's leg broke, so we slaughtered it. Then he said: "Gather the people of Madinah." Nafi' says: "I said: 'O Abu Abd al-Rahman, on what basis should I invite them? We do not even have bread." He said: "O Allah, all praise belongs to You. These are bones and this broth" — or he said: "Broth and meat" — "whoever wishes may eat and whoever wishes may leave."'"

Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrates that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Sayyiduna Ibrahim (peace and blessings be upon him) was circumcised at the age of eighty, at the place of Qudum, and he circumcised himself." Imam al-Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Qudum is not a place; rather it means 'eighty.'"

Umm al-Muhajir (may Allah have mercy on her) narrates: "I was brought as a captive among the slave-girls of Rome, and Sayyiduna Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) invited us to Islam. No one accepted Islam except me and one other woman. Then Sayyiduna Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Go, circumcise them and purify them.'"

Salim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrates that Sayyiduna Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) circumcised me and Nu'aym, and a ram was slaughtered on our behalf. We would take pride in this over the other boys, that a ram had been slaughtered on our behalf.

It is narrated by Umm 'Alqamah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the nieces of 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) were circumcised, so it was said to 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "Shall we not call someone to amuse them?" She said: "Very well." So a message was sent to 'Adiyy, and he came. When 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with him) passed by, she saw that he was singing and swaying about, and he had a great deal of hair. 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "Ugh! Drive out this Satan, drive him out!"

It is narrated by Aslam, the freedman of 'Umar (may Allah have mercy on him), that when we came to Syria with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him), the chieftain of that place came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have prepared food for you, and I would like you to honour me by coming to my home along with some distinguished companions. This would strengthen my resolve and also be an honour for me." 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "We cannot enter your churches with those images in them."

It is narrated by Umm Mahajir (may Allah have mercy on her), who said: "I and some other slave women were brought as captives from Rome. 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) invited us to Islam. So I and one other woman accepted Islam, but no one else did. 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: 'Have these two circumcised and purified.' Then I used to serve 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him)."

It is narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was circumcised when he was one hundred and twenty years old, and he lived for the remainder of that year. Sa'id (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Ibrahim (peace be upon him) was the first person to be circumcised, the first to host guests, the first to trim his moustache and clip his nails, and the first whose hair turned white. He said: "O my Lord, what is this?" Allah, the Most High, said: "This is dignity." Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: "O my Lord, increase me in dignity."

It is narrated by al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: "Are you not astonished at Malik ibn Mundhir, who went in search of nine newly converted Muslim farmers in Rome, examined them, and ordered that they be circumcised, even though it was winter (and wounds cause harm)? I came to know that some of them even died. Yet when the Romans and Ethiopians became Muslims during the time of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him), no examination was conducted of them (as to whether they had been circumcised or not)."
It is narrated by Ibn Shahab al-Zuhri (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: "When a person became Muslim, he was commanded to be circumcised, even if he was of advanced age."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 1 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1259
text:
Ja'far ibn Abi'l-Mughira said, "Sa'id ibn Jubayr stayed with me
and said tht Ibn 'Abbas related to me that he used to say, 'Where are those
who play with gambling arrows for the slaughtered camel? They buy a camel
with ten shares. Then they shuffle the arrows and it becomes nine shares
and they continue until comes down to one share. The others lose their
shares to the one share. That is gambling (arrow-shuffling).'"
Ibn 'Umar said, "Arrow-shuffling is gambling."

Rabi'a ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Hadir ibn 'Abdullah reported tht two
men wagered two cocks in the time of 'Umar. 'Umar ordered that the cock
be killed and a man of the Ansar said to him, "Will you kill a something
which glorifies Allah?" So 'Umar left it.

Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless
him and grant him peace, said, "If any of you makes an oath and swears
in his oath by al-Lat and al-'Uzza should say, 'There is no god but Allah.'
If any of you tells him companion, 'Come on, I will make a bet with you'
should give sadaqa."

Husayn ibn Mus'ab reported that someone told Abu Hurayra, "We
wager two pigeons and we do not want for there to be a third unwagered
pigeon between them so that the unwagered pigeon might take the winnings."
Abu Hurayra said, "That is how children behave. You are at the point where
you should abandon that."

It is related tht al-Bara' ibn Malik used to do the camel-chant
for the men and Anjasha used to do the camel-chant for the women. He had
a good voice and the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace,
said, "Anjasha, be gentle when you drive the glass-vessels."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 7 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1265
text:
Ibn 'Abbas said that the words of Allah in Luqman (35:6), "There
are people who trade in distracting tales" mean "singing and things
like it."

حَدَّثَنَا حَفْصُ بْنُ عُمَرَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا خَالِدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا عَطَاءُ بْنُ السَّائِبِ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، فِي قَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ‏:‏ ‏{‏وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَشْتَرِي لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ‏}‏، قَالَ‏:‏ الْغِنَاءُ وَأَشْبَاهُهُ‏.‏

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 8 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1266
text:
Al-Bara' ibn 'Azib reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah
bless him and grant him peace, said, "Extend the greeting and you will
be safe. The saw is evil."

Salman al-Ilhani reported that Fadala ibn 'Ubayd was in a gathering.
He heard that some people were playing backgammon. He got up in anger and
forbade it in the strongest possible terms. Then he said, "Anyone who plays
it in order to consume its winnings is like someone who eats pig meat and
does wudu' with blood."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 10 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1268
text:
Al-Fadil ibn Muslim reported that his father said, "When 'Ali,
may Allah be pleased with him, went out through the Bab al-Qasr, he saw
some backgammon players. He took them and locked them up from morning to
night. Some of them he only locked up for half the day. Those he locked
up until night were those who used silver. Those he locked up for half
the day were those who played it. He also commanded that they should not
be greeted."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 11 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1269
text:
Abu Musa al-Ash'ari reported that the Messenger of Allah, may
Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, "Anyone who plays backgammon
has rebelled against Allah and His Messenger."

'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud said, "Beware of these two marked cubes.
They should be forcibly prohibited. They are part of gambling."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 13 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1271
text:
Burayda reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant
him peace, said, "Someone who plays backgammon is like a person who puts
his hand in the meat and blood of a pig."

Abu Musa reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant
him peace, said, "Anyone who plays backgammon has rebelled against Allah
and His Messenger."

Nafi' related that if 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar found any of his family
playing backgammon, he would beat them and break the board.

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 16 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1274
text:
'Alqama ibn Abi 'Alqama reported from his mother that 'A'isha,
may Allah be pleased with her, heard that some people living in a room
in her house had a backgammon game. She sent to them, saying, "If you do
not remove it, I will evict you from my house." He censured them for playing
that.

Kulthum ibn Jabir said, "Ibn az-Zubayr addressed us and said,
'People of Makka, I have heard that there are men of Quraysh who play a
game called backgammon. It is done with the left hand. Allah says, 'Wine
and gambling.' (5:90) I swear by Allah that if anyone who plays it is brought
before me, I will punish him in his hair and skin, and I will give his
booty to the one who brings him to me."

Ya'la ibn Murra reported that he heard Abu Hurayra speaking about
someone who plays backgammon and bets on it, saying that he is like someone
who eats pig meat and that the person who plays it without betting on it
is like someone who washes his hands in pig's blood. The person who sits
looking at it is like someone who looks at pig's meat.

حَدَّثَنَا ابْنُ الصَّبَّاحِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا، عَنْ عُبَيْدِ بْنِ أَبِي أُمَيَّةَ الْحَنَفِيِّ هُوَ الطَّنَافِسِيُّ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنِي يَعْلَى أَبُو مُرَّةَ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ أَبَا هُرَيْرَةَ فِي الَّذِي يَلْعَبُ بِالنَّرْدِ قِمَارًا‏:‏ كَالَّذِي يَأْكُلُ لَحْمَ الْخِنْزِيرِ، وَالَّذِي يَلْعَبُ بِهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ الْقِمَارِ كَالَّذِي يَغْمِسُ يَدَهُ فِي دَمِ خِنْزِيرٍ، وَالَّذِي يَجْلِسُ عِنْدَهَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا كَالَّذِي يَنْظُرُ إِلَى لَحْمِ الْخِنْزِيرِ‏.‏

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 19 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1277
text:
'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said, "Someone who plays dice for
a bet is like a person who eats pig meat. Someone who plays it without betting
is like someone who washes his hands in pig's blood."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 20 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1278
text:
Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless
him and grant him peace, said, "A believer is not hurt by the same stone
twice."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 21 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1279
text:
Abu Hurayra reported that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and
grant him peace, said, "Anyone who shoots at night is not one of us."

Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless
him and grant him peace, said, "Anyone who bears arms against us is not
one of us."

in_book_reference: Book 54, Hadith 23 English translation : Book 54, Hadith 1281
text: Same hadith as 1280, but from Abu Musa.

It is narrated by Ya'la ibn Murrah (may Allah have mercy on him) that he heard Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) say regarding one who plays dice along with gambling: "He is like one who eats the flesh of a pig. And one who plays without gambling is like one who washes his hands in the blood of a pig. And one who sits by and watches is like one who looks at the flesh of a pig."

It is narrated by 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "One who plays dice with two dice is like one who eats the flesh of a pig, and one who plays with them without gambling is like one who washes his hands in the blood of a pig."
It is narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "A believer is not stung twice from the same hole."

It is narrated by Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "Whoever shoots arrows at us at night is not one of us." Abu 'Abdullah Imam al-Bukhari (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "Its chain is worthy of consideration."

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever takes up arms against us is not from among us."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1286 Arabic Hadith: 1286

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Whoever takes up weapons against us is not from among us."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1287 Arabic Hadith: 1287

It is narrated by the Companion of the Messenger, Abu 'Azah Yasar ibn 'Abd (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "When Allah, the Most High, wills for a servant to die in a certain land, He places for him some occupation in that place."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1288 Arabic Hadith: 1288

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he wiped his nose with a cloth and then said: "Woe, woe! Abu Hurayrah wipes his nose with cloth! I have found myself in a state of fainting between the chamber of Sayyidah A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) and the pulpit, due to hunger. The people (upon seeing this) would say: 'He is mad!' whereas nothing afflicted me except hunger."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1289 Arabic Hadith: 1289

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "O Messenger of Allah! We find in our hearts such whisperings that we would never utter them even if we were to be given all the wealth of the earth." He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Did you find such a thing in your hearts?" They said: "Yes." He said: "That is the clear and pure faith (iman)."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1290 Arabic Hadith: 1290

It is narrated by Shahr ibn Hawshab (may Allah have mercy on him) that I and my maternal uncle went to Sayyidah A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) and said: "One of us finds in his breast such thoughts that if he were to express them, his Hereafter would be ruined, and if they were to become apparent, he would be killed." She said that upon hearing this, she said 'Allahu Akbar' three times and said: "This was asked of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and he said: 'When such a situation befalls any one of you, let him say Allahu Akbar three times. Indeed, this awareness (of such whisperings) is not felt by anyone except a believer (mu'min).'"
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1291 Arabic Hadith: 1291

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "People will continue to ask about things that are not going to happen, until they will say: 'Allah is the Creator of all things, so who created Allah?'"
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1292 Arabic Hadith: 1292

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Beware of suspicion (su' al-zann), for suspicion is the most false of speech. Do not spy on one another, and do not compete with one another in worldly matters. Do not turn your backs on one another, and do not envy one another, and do not harbour hatred for one another. And be, O servants of Allah, brothers."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1293 Arabic Hadith: 1293

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) was with one of his wives when a man passed by. The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) called him and said: "O so-and-so! This is my wife, so-and-so." The man said: "I may suspect others, but I cannot suspect you." The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Indeed, Satan flows through the veins of the son of Adam like blood."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1294 Arabic Hadith: 1294

It is narrated by Sayyiduna 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) that the one whose property has been stolen continues to suspect others until he surpasses even the thief (in sin)."
Al-Adab Al-Mufrad Hadith: 1295 Arabic Hadith: 1295

It is narrated from Bilāl bin Sa'd al-Ash'arī (may Allah have mercy on him) that Mu'āwiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to Abū al-Dardā' (may Allah be pleased with him): "Write to me the names of the wicked (fāsiq) people of Damascus." He replied: "What concern do I have with the wicked of Damascus? How would I know them?" His son Bilāl (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "I shall write their names for you." So he wrote their names. Abū al-Dardā' (may Allah be pleased with him) asked: "How did you come to know about them? How did you find out that they are wicked, unless you are one of them? Therefore, write your own name first." And so he wrote the names but did not send them.

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1296*

It is narrated from 'Abd al-'Azīz bin Qays (may Allah have mercy on him) that I came to 'Abdullāh bin 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) while a slave-girl was trimming his hair. He said: "The powder or lotion used for removing hair softens the skin."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1297*

It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Five things are from among the acts of natural disposition (fiṭrah): circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, plucking the armpit hair, trimming the moustache, and cutting the nails."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1298*

It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Five things are from among the acts of natural disposition (fiṭrah): circumcision, shaving the pubic hair, cutting the nails, plucking the armpit hair, and trimming the moustache."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1299*

It is narrated from Abū Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "Five things are from among the acts of natural disposition (fiṭrah): cutting the nails, trimming the moustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and circumcision."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1300*

It is narrated from Abū Ṭufayl (may Allah be pleased with him) that I saw the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) distributing meat at the place of al-Ji'rānah, and at that time I was a young boy of nine years. I was picking up pieces of camel meat when a woman came to him, and he spread his cloak for her. I asked: "Who is this?" It was said: "This is the woman who nursed you, your (foster) mother."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1301*

It is narrated from al-Mughīrah bin Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him) that a man said: "May Allah reform the commander! Indeed, your gatekeeper gives preference in granting permission to those whom he recognizes." He said: "May Allah accept his excuse. Indeed, recognition (of those known) is beneficial even at the place of a biting dog or a charging camel (meaning that because of this, the gatekeeper does not allow strangers who might cause harm to approach those who are close and known)."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1302*

It is narrated from Ibrāhīm al-Nakha'ī (may Allah have mercy on him), who said: "Our companions used to permit us every form of play except (playing with) dogs." Abū 'Abdullāh, Imam al-Bukhārī (may Allah have mercy on him), said: "That is, (they permitted) children."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1303*

It is narrated from 'Abd al-'Azīz (may Allah have mercy on him) that a righteous elder known as Abū 'Uqbah informed me: "Once I passed along a road with Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and they passed by some Ethiopian children who were playing. He took out two dirhams and gave them to them."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1304*

It is narrated from 'Ā'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) used to send my friends to me, and they would play with me with dolls."

*Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1305*

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) saw a person chasing a pigeon. He (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "He is a devil chasing a she-devil."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1306 | Arabic Hadith: 1306

It is narrated by Sayyiduna al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) that he said: Sayyiduna Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) would invariably command in every blessed Jumu'ah sermon that dogs be killed and pigeons be slaughtered.
Through another chain of narration, it is narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri (may Allah have mercy on him) himself that Sayyiduna Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) used to command in his sermon the killing of dogs and the slaughtering of pigeons.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1307 | Arabic Hadith: 1307

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Zayd ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him) that one day Sayyiduna Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) came to his house and sought permission to enter. He (Zayd) granted him permission to enter, while his head was in the hands of a slave-girl who was combing it. He wished to remove his head from the slave-girl, but Sayyiduna Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Let her finish combing it." He submitted: "O Commander of the Faithful, you could have sent me a message and I would have come to you." Sayyiduna Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The matter was mine (and therefore it was more fitting that I should come myself)."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1308 | Arabic Hadith: 1308

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: When a person spits phlegm in front of people, he should conceal it with both his palms until his phlegm falls to the ground. And when a person is fasting, he should apply oil so that the effect of fasting is not visible upon him.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1309 | Arabic Hadith: 1309

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Habib ibn Abi Thabit (may Allah have mercy on him) that he liked that when a person speaks, he should not direct his attention towards any one individual, but rather address the gathering in a general manner.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1310 | Arabic Hadith: 1310

It is narrated by Ibn Abi Hazil (may Allah have mercy on him) that Sayyiduna Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) went with one of his companions to visit a sick person. When they entered the house, the people of the house began looking here and there. Sayyiduna Abdullah (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: "By Allah! If both your eyes were gouged out, it would be far better for you."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1311 | Arabic Hadith: 1311

It is narrated by Nafi' (may Allah have mercy on him) that some people from Iraq came to Sayyiduna Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both), and he noticed a gold necklace around the neck of one of their slave-girls, whereupon they began looking at one another. Sayyiduna Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "Your eyes are exceedingly sharp at seeing evil."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1312 | Arabic Hadith: 1312

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: There is no good in idle talk.
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1313 | Arabic Hadith: 1313

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "The worst and most wicked people of my Ummah are those who talk excessively, those who engage in boastful and ostentatious conversation, and those who speak with their mouths wide open. And the best people of my Ummah are those who are the most excellent in character."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1314 | Arabic Hadith: 1314

It is narrated by Sayyiduna Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: "Among the wicked is the one who practises duplicity — he says one thing to one group and goes to another group and says something else."
Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1315 | Arabic Hadith: 1315

Sayyidunā ʿAmmār ibn Yāṣir (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhumā) narrates that he heard the Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) saying: "Whoever is two-faced (a hypocrite) in this world, on the Day of Resurrection he will have two tongues of fire." Then a stout, heavy-built man passed by, and the Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said: "He is one of them."

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1316 | Arabic Hadith: 1316

in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 1 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1317
text:
Abu Hurayra reported that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless
him and grant him peace, said, "The person who is strong is not strong
because he can knock people down. The person who is strong is the one who
controls himself when he is angry."

in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 2 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1318
text:
Ibn 'Umar said, "There is nothing that is swallowed greater with
Allah in reward than a slave of Allah who swallows and contains his rancour
out of desire for the pleasure of Allah."

narrator: Sulayman ibn Surad said, "Two men abused one another in the presence of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and one of them began to get angry and his face got red. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, looked at him and said, 'I know some words that, if he says them, will remove this from him. They are:
in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 3 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1319
text: A variant of the previous hadith.

A variant of the previous hadith.

حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ بْنُ عُثْمَانَ قِرَاءَةً، عَنْ أَبِي حَمْزَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنِ ابْنِ ثَابِتٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ بْنِ صُرَدٍ قَالَ‏:‏ كُنْتُ جَالِسًا مَعَ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَرَجُلاَنِ يَسْتَبَّانِ، فَأَحَدُهُمَا احْمَرَّ وَجْهُهُ، وَانْتَفَخَتْ أَوْدَاجُهُ، فَقَالَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏:‏ إِنِّي لَأَعْلَمُ كَلِمَةً لَوْ قَالَهَا لَذَهَبَ عَنْهُ مَا يَجِدُ، فَقَالُوا لَهُ‏:‏ إِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم قَالَ‏:‏ تَعَوَّذْ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ، قَالَ‏:‏ وَهَلْ بِي مِنْ جُنُونٍ‏؟‏‏.‏

in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 5 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1320
text:
Ibn 'Abbas said, "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him
and grant him peace, said, ' Teach and make it easy. Teach and make it
easy.' three times. He went on, 'When you are angry, be silent' twice."

in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 6 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1321
text:
'Ali was heard to say to Ibn al-Kawwa', "Do you know what the
first one said? 'Loving the one you love is an easy matter. It may be that
one day he will be the one you hate. Hating the one who hate is an easy
matter. It may be that one day he will be the one you love.'"

حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مَرْوَانُ بْنُ مُعَاوِيَةَ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عُبَيْدٍ الْكِنْدِيُّ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ قَالَ‏:‏ سَمِعْتُ عَلِيًّا يَقُولُ لِابْنِ الْكَوَّاءِ‏:‏ هَلْ تَدْرِي مَا قَالَ الأَوَّلُ‏؟‏ أَحْبِبْ حَبِيبَكَ هَوْنًا مَا، عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ بَغِيضَكَ يَوْمًا مَا، وَأَبْغِضْ بَغِيضَكَ هَوْنًا مَا، عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونَ حَبِيبَكَ يَوْمًا مَا‏.‏

in_book_reference: Book 57, Hadith 7 English translation : Book 57, Hadith 1322
text:
Aslam said, " 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said, 'Do not let your love
be a total infatuation. Do not let your anger be destruction.' I asked,
'How is that?' He replied, 'When you love, you are infatuated like a child.
When you hate, you desire destruction for your companion.'"

حَدَّثَنَا سَعِيدُ بْنُ أَبِي مَرْيَمَ، قَالَ‏:‏ أَخْبَرَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، قَالَ‏:‏ حَدَّثَنَا زَيْدُ بْنُ أَسْلَمَ، عَنْ أَبِيهِ، عَنْ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ قَالَ‏:‏ لاَ يَكُنْ حُبُّكَ كَلَفًا، وَلاَ بُغْضُكَ تَلَفًا، فَقُلْتُ‏:‏ كَيْفَ ذَاكَ‏؟‏ قَالَ‏:‏ إِذَا أَحْبَبْتَ كَلِفْتَ كَلَفَ الصَّبِيِّ، وَإِذَا أَبْغَضْتَ أَحْبَبْتَ لِصَاحِبِكَ التَّلَف‏.‏

Sayyidunā Abū Hurayrah (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhu) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said: "The strong and brave one is not the one who overpowers (others in wrestling); rather, the truly strong one is the one who controls himself at the time of anger."

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1323 | Arabic Hadith: 1323

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿUmar (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhumā) narrates, and he said: "There is no drink that a person consumes which, in the sight of Allāh, carries greater reward and recompense than the drink that a person consumes seeking the pleasure of Allāh."

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1324 | Arabic Hadith: 1324

Sayyidunā Sulaymān ibn Ṣard (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhu) narrates, and he said: Two men reviled one another in the presence of the Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam), and one of them became so enraged that his face turned red. The Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam), upon seeing him, said: "Indeed, I know a word which, if this person were to say it, his anger would subside. (That word is): Aʿūdhu billāhi min al-Shayṭān al-Rajīm (I seek refuge in Allāh from the accursed Shayṭān)." So a man got up, went to that person, and said: "Do you know what the Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said? He said: 'You should recite: Aʿūdhu billāhi min al-Shayṭān al-Rajīm.'" That man replied: "Do you think I am insane?"

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1325 | Arabic Hadith: 1325

Sulaymān ibn Ṣard (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhu) narrates, and he said: I was sitting in the presence of the Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) and two men were reviling one another. The face of one of them turned red and his veins swelled. The Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said: "Indeed, I know a word which, if this person were to say it, all his anger would be extinguished." So the people said to him: "The Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said: 'Seek refuge in Allāh from the accursed Shayṭān.'" He replied: "Am I some madman?"

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1326 | Arabic Hadith: 1326

Sayyidunā Ibn ʿAbbās (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhumā) narrates that the Messenger of Allāh (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said: "Teach the people the religion and make things easy; teach and adopt the easy approach." The Prophet (ṣallAllāhu ʿalayhi wa sallam) said this three times, and then said: "And when you become angry, remain silent." He said this twice.

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1327 | Arabic Hadith: 1327

ʿUbayd al-Kindī (raḥimahullāh) narrates that he heard Sayyidunā ʿAlī (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhu) saying to Ibn Kawwāʾ: "Do you know what the early people used to say?" (He said:) "When you love someone, do not go to excess in your love, for it may be that one day that very person becomes your enemy. And when you harbour enmity towards someone, do not go to excess in your enmity, for it may be that one day that very person becomes your friend."

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1328 | Arabic Hadith: 1328

Sayyidunā ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (raḍiyAllāhu ʿanhu) narrates, and he said: "Let not your love drive you to madness, and let not your enmity drive you to destruction." I asked: "How is that?" He replied: "It is that when you love, you love with the reckless love of a child, taking everything to be solely for that person; and when you harbour enmity, you wish that your enemy be utterly destroyed."

Al-Adab al-Mufrad, Hadith: 1329 | Arabic Hadith: 1329
